idea.description: Add a cross-fitted recent directed-transition residual to per-dataset SASRec. Construct support from adjacent training interactions, shrink sparse rows toward a training-derived popularity prior, and combine it with neural scores using candidate-independent transforms. Establish fixed-weight fusion before testing a small evidence gate.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations outranking recent intent and upgrades lacking supporting evidence. Independent users’ observed next steps offer a testable, indirect signal for both failures, while providing no proof of ownership, compatibility, replacement need, or satisfaction. Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and negative lower-tail margin motivate testing improved candidate discrimination. Count features require cross-fitting because inclusive singleton transitions otherwise encode their own training labels.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain existing preprocessing, all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and SASREC_EPOCHS environment handling with host default 200. Write every artifact beneath the trial directory and run on one GPU. Use only permitted training interactions; titles/descriptions are optional for later work, while ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, and simulator traits are unavailable.

First train unchanged SASRec using its baseline loss, avoiding a simultaneous objective change. Assign training users deterministically to five folds using seed 42. For each fold, construct adjacent directed counts and item-frequency priors using only users outside that fold; build a separate deployment graph from all permitted training histories. Cross-fitted training examples must use their complementary graph, including its prior. This excludes the example’s own target contribution but does not enforce global chronology. Other users’ later training events can remain present; investigate chronological training-feature graphs only as an explicitly separate experiment without altering benchmark splits.

For a graph with counts C, let n[a]=sum_i C[a,i], f[i] be training item frequency, and p0[i]=f[i]/sum_j f[j] over nonpadding items. Define P(i|a)=(C[a,i]+lambda*p0[i])/(n[a]+lambda). Use the last W nonpadding prefix items, with recency weights proportional to rho^k and normalized over available anchors. Then q(H,i)=sum_k w_k P(i|a_k). For empty prefixes use p0; zero-outgoing-count anchors also yield p0. Store each row as sparse corrections C[a,i]/(n[a]+lambda) plus its scalar prior coefficient lambda/(n[a]+lambda). This preserves contributions to destinations absent from sparse rows. Initial CSR should retain all observed edges; top-K truncation, if needed, is an explicit approximation requiring a separate validation check and retained prior contribution.

Use s(H,i)=z_SASRec(H,i)+alpha*log1p(q(H,i)/tau), with tau=max(1/item_count,1e-12). This fixes neural temperature at one to avoid redundant scale tuning. Scores must be identical for an item regardless of which other candidates are supplied. Do not use candidate-set min–max normalization, z-scores, or separately normalized probability mixtures. Start with W=3, rho=0.7, lambda=10, and alpha=0; these are reproducible initial settings, not evidence-backed optima. Predeclare a small validation sweep alpha in {0,0.1,0.3,1.0}, sharing the same baseline checkpoint. If fusion is promising, separately compare lambda in {1,10,100}, W in {1,3}, and rho in {0.7,1.0}, avoiding an exhaustive joint search. Choose by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, break ties toward alpha=0 and then the simpler configuration, and log every evaluated configuration and GPU time within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

Fixed fusion can be validated directly without learning from graph-derived training features. Cross-fitting becomes mandatory when training the proposed gate or adapting neural parameters with the residual. For a gate experiment, initially freeze SASRec. Let g(H)=sigmoid(b+w^T e(H)) and replace alpha with alpha*g(H). Prefix-only features are log1p(history length), the recency-weighted log1p outgoing count of anchors, and agreement defined as the weighted fraction of anchor pairs sharing their highest-count outgoing destination; assign zero agreement when fewer than two anchors have outgoing edges. Fit feature means/scales on cross-fitted training prefixes only; use scale one for constant features. Initialize w=0 and b=-4. Candidate identities and validation targets must not enter gate inputs. Optimize baseline loss on cross-fitted scores, compare against the selected fixed residual, and serialize deployment graph statistics and the gate. Cross-fitting still creates a graph-size/support shift at deployment; compare feature distributions and do not claim it guarantees generalization.

Start without popularity correction. As a separate ablation, multiply q by clip((median_positive_frequency/max(f[i],1))^beta,0.5,2.0), with beta in {0,0.25}; recompute all transforms identically in training and inference. Test sixteen uniformly sampled negatives with sampled-softmax loss separately from graph/gate changes, excluding padding, target collisions, and known training-history positives. Unobserved items remain uncertain negatives. Larger margins and higher training support are insufficient selection criteria.

Controls should include unchanged SASRec, transition-only scoring, recency-weighted item-kNN, fixed residual fusion, and then the gate. Ablate direction using symmetrized counts, recency using equal anchor weights, popularity correction, and the count feature itself. Select practical controls before optional experiments to conserve budget. For the same sampled validation users/candidates, report raw transition coverage defined by any recent anchor having C[a,target]>0, supported/unsupported HR@10 with subgroup counts, inclusive versus cross-fitted training support, and Electronics’ margin tail. Subgroup metrics are explanatory and never replace macro HR@10.

The predictor writer must serialize the trained architecture, graph CSR/prior coefficients, fixed constants, gate and feature-standardization parameters, routing metadata, and item mappings beneath the trial directory. Score the complete unseen catalog in chunks and maintain global top-k; neural-only retrieval followed by reranking can omit fused winners. Preserve the baseline’s unseen-item filtering. Independently evaluated working/predict.py and diagnostic scoring must reproduce the same score formula.

Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions for batches (None, sequence, positive, negative) of shape B x L. view.model must be the actual deployed nn.Module, including gate parameters and registered scoring buffers where appropriate. Preserve view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. A feature container may hold neural states and prefix anchors, but adapt all probe consumers consistently. For training diagnostics, route reconstructed prefixes through cross-fitted graphs using deterministic prefix-to-fold metadata; exclude ambiguous duplicate prefixes from that diagnostic and report their count. Deployment scoring always uses the all-training graph. State clearly that embedding similarity measures the SASRec embedding component, while margin diagnostics measure combined scores. Missing category breakdowns must be marked unavailable; never infer unavailable categories or reviews. Continue supplying twenty real training users, five per category, with full-catalog unseen recommendations. Validation improvements remain specific to the pinned 200-users/category, 99-unique-negatives, evaluation-seed-42 protocol and do not demonstrate full-catalog gains.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset independently:
    train baseline SASRec with original seeds, splits, and environment defaults
    assign users to five deterministic folds
    for fold r:
        graph[r] = adjacent_counts_and_item_prior(users outside fold r)
    deployment_graph = adjacent_counts_and_item_prior(all training users)

support(graph, prefix, item):
    anchors = last W nonpadding prefix items
    if anchors empty: return graph.p0[item]
    weights = normalize([rho**k for k in recency order])
    return sum_k weights[k] * (
        graph.C[anchors[k], item] / (graph.n[anchors[k]] + lambda)
        + lambda * graph.p0[item] / (graph.n[anchors[k]] + lambda)
    )

score(prefix, item, graph):
    q = support(graph, prefix, item)
    residual = log1p(q / max(1 / item_count, 1e-12))
    coefficient = alpha
    if optional_gate_enabled:
        evidence = standardized_prefix_only_features(prefix, graph)
        coefficient *= sigmoid(b + dot(w, evidence))
    return SASRec_score(prefix, item) + coefficient * residual

Fixed-fusion experiment:
    freeze baseline checkpoint
    evaluate preregistered alpha values using deployment_graph
    choose using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10

Optional gate experiment:
    initialize w=0, b=-4; initially freeze SASRec
    for each training user's causal prefixes:
        graph = graph[user_fold]
        fit baseline loss using combined positive/negative scores
    validate with deployment_graph

Separate controls:
    compare transition-only, item-kNN, direction/recency/correction ablations
    test 16-negative sampled softmax without silently combining changes
    record subgroup coverage, margins, macro HR@10, and resource use

Serialize complete scoring state and update predictor writer.
For final full-catalog recommendations:
    use deployment_graph
    score every unseen candidate in chunks with exactly the same itemwise formula
    maintain global top-k

originality.positive: Cross-fitted support and candidate-independent deployment make the adaptation methodologically sharper and directly test the diagnosed failures.
originality.negative: Directed transitions, recency weighting, additive fusion, shrinkage, and cross-fitting are established ingredients; this is an empirical adaptation rather than a new model family.

future_potential.positive: Provides an auditable framework for investigating when independent transition evidence helps current-intent ranking and when learned fusion overfits.
future_potential.negative: Sparse pair coverage limits the count component, compatibility remains unobserved, and improvements under sampled evaluation may not transfer to full-catalog recommendation.

code_difficulty.positive: Fixed fusion uses sparse counts and a small scoring extension without external encoders or pretrained weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable cross-fitting, dense-prior preservation, diagnostic routing, exact chunked inference, and optional gating add substantial work beyond a simple residual.

report:
### Insights and framework

Three starting-point insights guide the proposal. First, SASRec may mix recent and older interests; explicit recent evidence could reduce intent dilution. Second, isolated interactions establish neither equipment ownership nor replacement needs; behavioral transitions cannot verify compatibility. Third, Electronics has 14.95% wrong sampled rankings and a −0.4812 lower-tail margin, motivating experiments without implying validation gains.

Three literature insights sharpen the design. [GaGNN](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2024.120623) motivates training-derived relationships; [LSIDN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) motivates separate preference timescales, with uncertain sparse-history transfer. [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) motivates loss controls; larger margins alone need not improve ranking. [FPMC](https://archives.iw3c2.org/www2010/pub/pdfs/RendleFreudenthaler2010-FPMC.pdf) and [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) establish that additive preference/transition fusion has substantial precedent.

The conceptual map retains three directions: **temporal evidence** (recent/sustained interests), **relational evidence** (observed transitions/broad associations), and **optimization** (negative coverage/false-negative exposure). A methodological gap crosses them: target-inclusive transition statistics can create shortcuts, analogous to [target-edge leakage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00899).

### Candidate assessment

Each cell gives score/10, strength (+), and limitation (−). Difficulty increases with effort.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Recent/history pooling gate [LSIDN] | 3; +compact; −established | 6; +reusable; −sparse evidence | 7; +intent; −compatibility unknown | 5; +context; −indirect effect | 3; +small branch; −writer changes |
| **Cross-fitted recent transition residual** [GaGNN, FPMC] | 3; +leakage control; −established fusion | 6; +auditable; −limited pair coverage | 7; +specific next steps; −ownership unproven | 6; +discrimination; −unseen pairs | 5; +sparse operations; −cross-fitting parity |
| Sixteen-negative sampled softmax [gSASRec] | 2; +clean control; −established | 7; +strong baseline; −protocol dependence | 4; +ranking; −intent implicit | 8; +confusion; −false negatives | 3; +simple loss; −extra scoring |

### Selected idea: recent transition residual

At 0% progress, retain this reversible extension, beginning with fixed fusion before learning a gate. It targets **broad relevance outranking recent intent** and **unsupported upgrades** through specific independently observed next steps. The latter remains an indirect hypothesis: transitions cannot establish compatibility or satisfied needs. It also targets Electronics’ weak separation tail.

Build adjacent transition counts from training histories. Use five user-grouped folds so training features exclude the target user’s entire fold. Smooth each row toward a training-derived item-frequency prior; retain its dense prior contribution outside stored edges. Use fixed itemwise transforms, never candidate-set normalization. Start without popularity correction; test clipped correction separately because it amplifies rare-edge noise.

```text
fit SASRec with its baseline loss
build five complementary training graphs and one deployment graph
score(prefix,item) = neural_score + alpha * log1p(support(prefix,item)/tau)
select fixed fusion constants using pinned macro validation HR@10
only then test an evidence gate or 16-negative softmax separately
```

Cross-fitting reduces self-label shortcuts but does not enforce global chronology; retain pinned splits and test chronological training-feature construction separately. Compare unchanged SASRec, transition-only, recency item-kNN, and fixed fusion before gating. Ablate direction, recency, correction, and count features. Report support coverage and supported/unsupported validation HR@10, plus Electronics’ margin tail. Preserve all four routes, seeds, diagnostic interfaces, and identical full-catalog scoring. Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog gains ([Rendle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263)); no improvement is claimed before evaluation.
